I will keep my land in the pattern I trust most here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields, and I will keep a small piece in spring peanut. I do that because grain is the safest choice for me. Wheat and maize fit the local weather, the water and fertilizer needs are familiar, and I know how to manage them without taking big risks. I do not want to chase fancy crops that need more skill, more labor, or uncertain buyers. I would rather have steady harvests and cash flow than gamble.

For the main land, I will first take care of the winter wheat that is already in the ground at the start of the season. I will use improved seed wheat, topdress nitrogen in spring, give a few irrigations if water is available, and spray only when disease or aphids become a real problem. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize on the same area, because that rotation is the backbone of farming here and makes the best use of the year. For maize I will use hybrid seed, give enough nitrogen for a strong ear, and keep irrigation and pesticide use moderate. On a smaller piece, I will plant spring peanut because it spreads my risk a little, gives me some cash, and does not need as much water as maize. I will keep tillage simple with rotary tillage on most land, because it is cheaper and faster for me than deep ploughing every time.
